chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad Abu Abdullah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said, and the room was full with his family members: 'Know that he is not from us, the one who does not have good neighbourliness with those who are in his neighbourhood.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of good neighbourliness in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links neighbourly rights (huquq al-jiran) directly to identity within the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing good conduct as a definitive criterion of spiritual lineage. This reflects the Shia emphasis on social ethics as an extension of theological fidelity, where the 'household' extends beyond kinship to include those in close proximity. The phrase 'the house is filled with its people' underscores the intimate, domestic nature of these rights, making neighbourly kindness a practical manifestation of faith.
